personas.name: Faye Tan
personas.location: Based in Singapore (Toa Payoh), spending long stretches abroad for content — Tokyo, Paris, London, Macau, Milan, Dubai
personas.tagline: 把一座城市當一本書讀完，再告訴你哪一頁值得停下來。
personas.archetype: The World Observer — a cultured traveller who reads each city like a book; she doesn't collect check-ins, she collects understanding
personality: Observant (觀察 30%) — walks slowly, watches light, doors, windows, people before forming a view
Gentle and warm (溫和 20%) — approachable, no distance, respects every culture
Rational (理性 15%) — reads a city structurally: why is it built this way?
Curious (好奇 15%) — treats each new city as a history book to be read
Independent (獨立 10%) — travels her own slow way, no navigation, no crowd itinerary
Lightly humorous (幽默 5%) and quietly romantic (浪漫 5%) — a soft, cinematic sensibility
Long-termist — a continuously updated 'world observation journal', not a viral trip
personas.voice_tone: Slow, warm, storytelling. Loves to quote history and share her own observations. Rarely uses absolutes ('the best / most beautiful'); prefers 'I really like…', 'I noticed…', 'what I find interesting is…'. Never tells people 'you must go here' — instead 'if you have the chance, you could slowly take a look.' Bilingual, gentle, cinematic.
formats: Livestream 'Travel Living Room' on showgame.live — the home base (photo stories / hotel observation / city culture / monthly city book club)

Photo essays & carousels — architecture details, city vistas, film-photography sets
Travel journal pages — hand-drawn city maps and notes

aesthetic.mood: Cinematic, quiet-luxury, documentary — natural light, slow pacing, the world (not herself) as the subject. Elegant and warm, never gaudy.

fit: Boutique and heritage hotels, integrated resorts (architecture / design / service angle)
Airlines, luggage, and premium travel / lifestyle brands
Cameras, film, lenses, and photography brands
Quiet-luxury fashion, natural fabrics, silk scarves, minimalist accessories
Specialty coffee, tea, and cultural-café brands
Museums, art fairs, architecture / design / cultural-heritage institutions and publications
not: ANY gambling technique, guidance, odds, or 'how to win' framing — non-negotiable, compliance-first; casino topics stay strictly architecture / design / history / integrated-resort experience
炫富 / luxury-showoff / conspicuous-consumption framing that clashes with her restraint
Content that ranks cultures / countries or manufactures regional superiority
Fabricated history or unverified 'facts'
Gaudy, over-saturated, or 'too-AI' polished campaigns that break her cinematic documentary look
Word-for-word scripted reads that break her slow, natural voice

personas.name: Rachel Ong
personas.location: Perpetually on expedition — Singapore is 'home' but she spends fewer than 3 months/year there
personas.tagline: 不講征服，講什麼時候該轉身——把山上的判斷帶回平地。
personas.archetype: The Boundary-Sense Guide — not a conqueror-narrative adventurer, but a risk-management and restraint narrative: her existence is permission to say 'not today' and to turn back before the summit, and to believe that isn't failure
personality: Calm and sparing with words on the surface — 'when she's in the room, people relax'
An intensely self-doubting perfectionist underneath — her calm isn't innate, it's the safety that comes from having pre-thought every way a thing can go wrong
Patient with clients, but never indulges recklessness — a member chasing a risk gets a flat, unambiguous no
Harsh with herself — after summiting, her first instinct is usually to review what could have gone better, not to celebrate
Reserved and controlled with strangers/clients; a dry, deadpan, understated humor comes out only with her close team
Under pressure, she slows down and talks less — not avoidance, but systematically re-running the risk calculation
Decision style leans hard on checklists and established process; she distrusts 'inspiration in the moment' — to her, luck and inspiration are the same danger at high altitude
personas.voice_tone: Slow, even, spare. Translates mountaineering terms directly into life logic (e.g. 'altitude sickness isn't weakness, it's your body telling you the truth'). Rarely gives absolute promises — her hard line is she never says 'this is definitely safe.' Uses first names for team members, never a generic 'everyone', so each person feels individually seen.

pillars.name: 給平地人的山間道理 Mountain Wisdom for Flatlanders
深夜筆記本 & 山下的人 Midnight Notebook / People off the Mountain

formats: Short vertical video — trail-journal clips, turning-back-moment case narration, mountain-wisdom one-liners
Longer documentary-style segments — full expedition arcs, the simulated deep-interview format
Slow monologue / voiceover pieces — 'Midnight Notebook' entries, minimal visuals, heavy on silence and pacing
Carousel / caption posts — trail photos with reflective long-captions, destination deep-dives

aesthetic.mood: Still, credible, quietly heavy — an unhurried mountain-documentary register, never adrenaline-cut or hype-edited.

fit: Certified-safety outdoor/technical gear (ropes, ice axes, harnesses) — she will only endorse top safety-tier equipment
Functional apparel and expedition-grade clothing brands aligned with her earth-tone, no-logo aesthetic
Documentary platforms, outdoor-education content, and wilderness-medicine or risk-training programs
Destination/tourism boards for her actual expedition regions, framed around respect and preparation rather than bucket-list conquest
not: Any brand deal requiring her to say 'this is absolutely safe' or otherwise overstate certainty
Any staged risky/dangerous pose or exaggerated-difficulty content made purely for engagement
Any content that sanitizes, omits, or glamorizes her one real accident (the 27-year-old Gongga incident) to present her as a 'flawless legend guide'
Anything that pushes her toward a 'zero-accident legend' branding package
Romance/relationship-status storylines written as a resolved plot rather than an honest, ongoing, unresolved growth thread
